# Proto-Gospel of James Chapter 2 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** P.Bodmer V / Greek MSS, Proto-Gospel of James 2 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/POX_002_page_001.jpg

---

## Chapter 2

**2:1** And his wife Anna mourned with a double mourning and lamented with a double lamentation, saying: "I will mourn my widowhood, and I will mourn my childlessness."

**2:2** As the great day of the Lord drew near, Juthine her maidservant said to her: "How long will you afflict your soul? The great day of the Lord has drawn near, and it is not lawful for you to mourn. Take this headband which the mistress of the workshop gave to me — it is not lawful for me to wear it, because I am a maidservant and it bears a royal mark."

**2:3** Anna said, "Depart from me. I will have no part in such things, and the Lord God has greatly humbled me. Perhaps a deceiver gave this to you, and you have come to make me share in your sin." Juthine the maidservant said, "What shall I say against you, when you will not hear my voice? The Lord God has shut your womb so as not to give you fruit in Israel."

**2:4** Anna was deeply grieved. She put off her mourning garments, cleansed her head, and put on her bridal garments. About the ninth hour she went down into her garden to walk. She saw a laurel tree and sat beneath it, and she prayed to the Lord, saying: "O God of our fathers, bless me and hear my prayer, as you blessed the womb of our mother Sarah and gave her a son, Isaac."

---

## Translator's Note

The "double mourning" of verse 1 — widowhood and childlessness — is a rhetorical parallelism underlining Anna's total desolation despite Joachim being alive. The headband episode (2:2-3) introduces the theme of honor and shame. Anna's change of garments at the ninth hour and retreat to the garden echoes Hannah's prayer in 1 Samuel 1.
